candidates.rationale: A prices quality against where the high sits inside its own 21-day range of highs; B prices the volume-range coupling. The fusion is a normaliser: A donates TS_MEAN($high, 21) as a price scale, B donates $high - $low as the risk numerator, and their ratio turns a raw dollar range into a scale-free relative range that neither parent can express (A has no range at all; B only sees the range through a correlation, which is already scale-invariant and therefore blind to the range LEVEL). Quality is then netted against that relative range, giving a limits-to-arbitrage spread: long high-ROA names that are quiet relative to their own price, short volatile ones. Both parent subtrees are kept at exactly 3 nodes so neither the 4-node archive gate nor the guarded-denominator trap is tripped (A's own TS_MAX($high, 21) + 1e-8 is a 5-node subtree and is deliberately not reused).

This is a weak pair and I would rather say so than dress it up. A and B are not really two ideas: both compute a rolling correlation between the intraday range and a volume series (volume at 21d, dollar volume at 42d), and those two volume series collapse into each other. The genuine term-structure cross - short-horizon coupling minus long-horizon coupling - is also unbuildable, because reusing either TS_CORR whole is a 6-node share and an instant archive rejection, and each parent's only legal 3-node donation is the same subtree, $high - $low. So the child drops the redundant kernel instead of forcing it: it keeps $high - $low (satisfying both parents) and combines the one non-overlapping thing B has, the earnings-quality leg, with a range regime measured against its own history rather than against volume. The conditioning claim is that accrual quality is priced harder when ranges are expanding relative to their 3-month norm. B's fundamental spread itself is a 5-node subtree and cannot be donated, so only the accrual axis is carried.

Interaction plus a combined quality axis. A donates $high - $low, B donates TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 10); their cross-sectional rank difference is an Amihud-style price-impact measure - wide relative range on thin recent dollar volume - which A only ever sees as a 42-day time-series correlation and B only as a volume level with no volatility term at all. The fundamental leg fuses both parents' quality axes into one score (efficiency up, accruals down), using the two fields that clear the coverage gate. Scale-free by construction: the range is divided by the high and the volume enters as a within-name 10-day rank, so neither leg is a disguised price-level or market-cap sort.

Same two parents as the previous pair, so this takes the dynamic view rather than the level view. B's 42-day correlation uses raw dollar volume, which is dominated by price level and market cap; substituting A's 10-day TS_RANK of dollar volume makes the liquidity leg a within-name state variable, so the correlation now measures whether volatility arrives WITH liquidity or without it - a scale-free volatility-liquidity coupling that B's raw-dollar version cannot isolate and that A never computes, since A only reads the dollar-volume rank as a static level. Tilted by A's asset-turnover. Donations: TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 10) from A, $high - $low from B, both exactly 3 nodes.

A change of risk axis. B risk-adjusts its lagged momentum by dividing by that name's own return volatility, a per-name time-series scaling; the child instead nets the momentum rank against a cross-sectional rank of range volatility normalised by price level, so risk becomes a comparison across names rather than a division within one. That makes the factor a two-sided spread - long cheap-volatility winners, short expensive-volatility ones - which neither parent produces: A has no price trend, B has no notion of relative risk. B donates DELAY($close, 21), A donates $high - $low; A's fundamental spread is a 5-node subtree and cannot legally be carried. Windows are shifted off B's 147 so the guarded denominator DELAY($close, 147) + 1e-8 is not reproduced. Adjusted and raw price scales are kept in separate self-consistent ratios.

A signed interaction, not a weighting. B's CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) is centred at zero, so multiplying it into A's lagged momentum flips the sign of the momentum for low-quality names: the child is long momentum in high-ROE names and short it in low-ROE ones. Neither parent holds that - A has no fundamentals, B has no price trend, and a plain CS_RANK weight in [0,1] could only attenuate momentum, never reverse it. B's relative-range risk term is kept as a separate additive charge at a different scale, replacing A's return-volatility denominator with an intraday one. Donations: DELAY($close, 21) from A, CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) from B. B's Delta-leverage leg is deliberately not carried: $leverage sits at the edge of the coverage gate and profitability-minus-leverage is already a saturated shape in the archive.

Both parents carry a volatility estimate, but of different kinds, and that is the whole cross. A's TS_STD($return, 105) is close-to-close; B's $high - $low is intraday. Measured over the same 105-day window and differenced in rank space, what survives is the volatility NOT produced during the session - overnight and gap risk - which neither parent can express: A only divides by total volatility, B only correlates the raw range against turnover-scaled volume. The spread is then conditioned on B's ROE rank, so it reads as quality-conditioned gap risk. TS_STD($return, 105) is used bare rather than as a guarded denominator, because A's TS_STD($return, 105) + 1e-8 is a 5-node subtree and reusing it would be an automatic archive rejection; B's turnover leg is likewise unusable, its $dollar_volume / ($open + 1e-8) being 5 nodes.

These two parents are near-siblings - both are quality minus a range-based risk term - so the room is narrow and worth stating. What separates them is only how each scales the range: B correlates it with turnover-scaled volume, A divides it by a 42-day mean open. Neither ever relates the range to the price LEVEL itself, so that is the cross: A donates TS_MEAN($open, 42), B donates $high - $low, and putting them in one TS_CORR gives an asymmetric-volatility (leverage-effect) measure - does this name's range widen as its price rises or as it falls - which is a risk characteristic neither parent computes. Tilted by ROE. A's guarded normaliser TS_MEAN($open, 42) + 1e-8 is 5 nodes and is not reused; the 42-day mean appears only as a correlation argument.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: CROSSOVER. Each pair below holds two parents from DIFFERENT archive
niches. Return one child per pair that genuinely combines them.

A child must keep a complete sub-expression of at least 3 nodes

interaction. If you cannot name one, the pair is a bad cross and you should say
